title: A Fall-to-Winter Day Trip From Seoul: Gapyeong's Garden of Morning Calm, Petite France, and Nami Island
html:
If you want one easy day trip from Seoul that works for both autumn leaves and winter lights, Gapyeong (가평) in Gyeonggi-do is hard to beat. It's about an hour from Seoul by train, and in one day you can walk through a famous garden, take a few silly photos in a tiny "French village," and stroll the tree-lined island made famous by the K-drama Winter Sonata — with a riverside coffee stop and a no-reservation dinner built into the route.

Getting From Seoul to Gapyeong

The easiest way in is the ITX-Cheongchun train, a reserved-seat express that runs from Yongsan or Cheongnyangni station in Seoul to Gapyeong Station or Cheongpyeong Station in about 50–70 minutes. Book seats ahead on the Korail app (Korail Talk) or at the station, since it sells out on weekends. From either station, local buses and taxis connect to the sights below — most Korean tourists actually drive or join a small shared van tour for the day, since the three stops aren't within walking distance of each other.

If you'd rather not plan bus transfers yourself, look up a "가평 1일 투어" (Gapyeong one-day tour) shuttle online — these are minivans that loop between Gapyeong-area attractions on a fixed schedule and are popular with both locals and tourists for exactly this kind of multi-stop day trip.

On the way between stops, it's worth stopping for coffee: the stretch along Cheongpyeong Lake, near Cheongpyeong Station, has several large, window-facing cafes built for the view — look up "청평 카페" (Cheongpyeong cafe) on Naver Map or Kakao Map when you're in the area, since smaller local cafes open and close often and a live map search is more reliable than any fixed list.

Stop 1 – The Garden of Morning Calm: Autumn Color by Day, Winter Lights by Night

The Garden of Morning Calm (아침고요수목원) is a large themed botanical garden with more than twenty separate garden areas. In autumn (usually mid-October through early November), the maples and the garden's famous "Sunken Garden" flower beds turn deep red and gold. In winter, the whole garden reopens after dark as the "Five-Color Starlight Garden" Lighting Festival (오색별빛정원전) — one of Korea's best-known light festivals, with the paths and trees strung in colored LEDs.

The light festival normally runs from early December to mid-March, with evening hours roughly 17:00–21:00 (later on Saturdays). Exact dates shift slightly each year, so check the garden's official site or call 1544-6703 close to your visit. Daytime hours are 08:30–19:00 most of the year and 10:00–21:00 in winter (December–March), so you can actually see both the autumn-style daylight garden and the night lights on the same visit once the festival starts. Parking is free and the garden is open every day of the year.

Stop 2 – Petite France: A Quick, Quirky Photo Break

Petite France (쁘띠프랑스) is a small, brightly painted "French village" theme park built around the story of The Little Prince. It's not trying to be an authentic recreation of France — think of it more as a photo-friendly stop with doll museums, craft workshops, and a few European-style cafes, best enjoyed with low expectations and a camera. Most visitors spend 1–2 hours here, which makes it an easy middle stop between the garden and the island. It's open 09:00–18:00 year-round (with occasional evening hours — check the website), and there's an entrance fee at the gate.

Stop 3 – Nami Island: The Famous Metasequoia Lane

Nami Island (남이섬) is a small, crescent-shaped island on the Bukhangang (North Han River) — technically just across the border in Gangwon-do, but grouped into most Gapyeong day trips because it's so close by. It's most famous for its Metasequoia Lane, a long row of tall, straight trees that turn a striking orange-brown in late autumn and became internationally known after the K-drama Winter Sonata was filmed there — it's one of the most-photographed tree paths in Korea.

You reach the island only by a short ferry from Gapyeongnaru Pier (round-trip ticket included with island admission), running roughly every 10–30 minutes from 08:00–21:00. Once inside, it's flat and easy to explore on foot or by renting a bike, and there's enough to see (a bird garden, craft center, and wood-fired pizza-making experience) to fill 2–3 hours comfortably.

Where to eat near the pier: Right by Gapyeongnaru Pier (a 5-minute walk, before you even take the ferry), there are a few dakgalbi (닭갈비 — spicy stir-fried marinated chicken, grilled at your table) restaurants that don't require a reservation to walk in, which makes them an easy dinner stop after the island. A quick heads-up for first-timers: dakgalbi is genuinely spicy, so ask for it mild ("안 맵게" — "an maep-ge") if you're not used to Korean spice levels, or order a side of plain rice and egg to cool it down. On the island itself, Nami Island also runs its own small food court with Korean, Chinese, Japanese, and Western options, which has historically included vegetarian dishes — worth checking current signage or asking staff for today's menu, since food stalls do change over time.

Suggested One-Day Timeline

Here's one realistic way to fit all three stops into a single day without rushing too much:

Time Stop What to Do
07:30–09:00 Seoul → Gapyeong/Cheongpyeong ITX-Cheongchun train from Yongsan or Cheongnyangni
09:30–11:30 Garden of Morning Calm Walk the themed gardens; stay later in winter for the Lighting Festival
12:00–13:00 Cheongpyeong Lake area Lunch or coffee at a lakeview cafe
13:30–15:00 Petite France Photos, Little Prince exhibits, quick walk-through
15:30–18:00 Nami Island Ferry over, walk the Metasequoia Lane, bike or stroll the island
18:00–19:00 Gapyeongnaru Pier Walk-in dakgalbi dinner near the pier
19:30–21:00 Gapyeong/Cheongpyeong → Seoul Return ITX-Cheongchun or local train

If that feels too packed, it's completely fine to drop Petite France and spend the extra time relaxing at Nami Island or the Garden of Morning Calm instead — most locals who do this route pick two of the three stops rather than rushing through all three.

Practical Tips for First-Time Visitors

  • Dress in layers: Gapyeong is noticeably colder than Seoul in late autumn and winter, especially outdoors at the Garden of Morning Calm after dark and on the open ferry to Nami Island.
  • Check the Lighting Festival dates before you go: the exact start/end dates move slightly each year, so confirm on the garden's official site rather than an old blog post.
  • Buy train tickets in advance: the ITX-Cheongchun has reserved seating only and regularly sells out on weekends, especially during peak foliage weeks and the light festival season.
  • Bring cash or a Korean-friendly card: smaller cafes and food stalls in this area don't always take foreign cards.
  • Use Naver Map or Kakao Map, not Google Maps: these are far more accurate for bus routes, live traffic, and up-to-date cafe/restaurant hours in Korea.

💬 Planning a Gapyeong day trip, or not sure how to split your time between these three stops? Ask in the comments — happy to help plan your route!
